clinicalPearls: A distal arthrogryposis defined by the combination of camptodactyly, talipes equinovarus and cleft palate (or bifid uvula/submucous cleft)
Short stature is a frequent feature, distinguishing it from other distal arthrogryposis subtypes
Ptosis and downslanting palpebral fissures may be present
Associated with variants in PIEZO2, a mechanosensitive ion channel, in the distal arthrogryposis 3/5 spectrum, inherited autosomal dominant
The cleft palate mandates early feeding support and coordinated cleft-team surgical repair
Management combines physiotherapy and splinting for the limbs with staged palatal and orthopaedic surgery
reference.pathophysiology: Gordon syndrome sits within the PIEZO2-related distal arthrogryposis spectrum. PIEZO2 encodes a mechanically activated ion channel important for proprioception and touch, and gain-of-function variants disturb sensory feedback and muscle tone during foetal development. Impaired and unbalanced foetal movement permits periarticular fibrosis and joint contracture, giving camptodactyly and clubfoot, while abnormal palatal shelf development produces the cleft palate. The contractures are congenital and static rather than progressive, and the phenotype overlaps with distal arthrogryposis type 5.
additionalDifferentials: Distal arthrogryposis type 5 (also PIEZO2-related, with ophthalmoplegia)
Van der Woude syndrome when cleft palate predominates
Isolated cleft palate with associated limb anomalies
additionalInvestigations: Dysmorphology assessment and careful palatal examination for overt or submucous cleft
Molecular genetic testing for PIEZO2 and a distal arthrogryposis panel
Radiographs of hands, feet and spine and assessment of growth/stature
Prenatal ultrasound for foetal akinesia in at-risk pregnancies
Ophthalmology review for ptosis and eye movement abnormalities
redFlags: Feeding difficulty and aspiration risk from cleft palate in the neonate
Airway concerns associated with micrognathia or ptosis-related features
Marked short stature prompting endocrine and skeletal review
reference.prognosis: With cleft repair, feeding support and orthopaedic management the outlook is good; intellect and lifespan are usually normal, though short stature and residual limb deformity may persist and speech may require support after palatal surgery.
pitfalls: Missing a submucous cleft palate or bifid uvula in a child presenting with limb contractures
Overlooking the PIEZO2 spectrum overlap with distal arthrogryposis type 5
Neglecting short stature and its follow-up

management: Repair the cleft palate through a coordinated cleft team, with early specialised feeding support for the palatal defect
Manage camptodactyly and talipes equinovarus with serial casting, splinting, physiotherapy and corrective orthopaedic surgery
Provide physiotherapy and occupational therapy to maximise joint mobility and hand function for the static congenital contractures
Offer speech and language therapy after palatal repair and monitor for velopharyngeal insufficiency and hearing
Review for ptosis with ophthalmology and monitor growth given the frequent short stature
Coordinate multidisciplinary genetics, orthopaedic and cleft-team care, and offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant PIEZO2 inheritance
